title: Open Source Software
text: I build and maintain open-source tools that democratize access to economic data across Latin America. These packages are designed for researchers, analysts, and policymakers working on development economics, social policy evaluation, and quantitative research.

title: Open Source Software
section: Python Packages for Latin American Data
text:
Python Packages for Latin American Data
enahodata — Peru Household Survey Access
   
GitHub · PyPI
Python package for simplified access to Peru’s National Household Survey (ENAHO) microdata. Download, process, and analyze data on poverty, employment, education, health, and household characteristics using pandas-compatible functions.

usebcrp — Central Reserve Bank of Peru API
   
GitHub · PyPI
Python client for the Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP) statistical API. Programmatic access to macroeconomic indicators, monetary policy data, and national accounts with pandas integration.

usecasen — Chile Socioeconomic Survey Tools
   
GitHub · PyPI
Python tools for working with Chile’s National Socioeconomic Characterization Survey (CASEN). Facilitates multidimensional poverty analysis and social policy evaluation.

usebcch — Central Bank of Chile Database Client
   
GitHub · PyPI
Python client for the Central Bank of Chile’s statistical database. Retrieve time series data on inflation, GDP, exchange rates, financial indicators, and external sector statistics.

title: Open Source Software
text:
Stata Packages
enahotools — ENAHO Data Processing for Stata
 
GitHub
Stata package for processing and analyzing Peru’s National Household Survey (ENAHO). Automated data cleaning, variable labeling, and survey-weighted estimation commands.

title: Open Source Software
text:
Impact & Philosophy
These packages are part of my commitment to open science and data democratization. By lowering barriers to access public data, I aim to enable more rigorous research and evidence-based policymaking across Latin America.
All tools are open-source (MIT License), actively maintained, and built with reproducibility in mind.

text: This study examines the causal effect of resource-related social conflicts on educational outcomes in Peru, using a difference-in-differences design with event-study specification.

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text: This study examines the causal effect of resource-related social conflicts on educational outcomes in Peru, using a difference-in-differences design with event-study specification.

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Research Question
Do mining and hydrocarbon conflicts disrupt human capital accumulation in affected communities?

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Methodology
Causal Inference Strategy: - Event study with staggered treatment adoption - Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) DID estimator - Shift-share instrumental variables for robustness checks - Two-way fixed effects regression with clustered standard errors
Data Sources: - Administrative education records (MINEDU) - Social conflict registry (National Police & Ombudsman’s Office) - Mining production and canon transfers (MEF) - Census data for demographic controls

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Key Findings

Exposure to social conflicts reduces standardized test scores by 0.15 SD
Dropout rates increase by 2.3 percentage points in affected districts
Effects persist for 3+ years after conflict occurrence
Stronger impacts in rural areas and communities with weak governance

title: Social Conflicts and Human Capital Accumulation
text:
Policy Implications
Results suggest the need for: - Targeted educational interventions in conflict-affected areas - Improved conflict prevention mechanisms in extractive zones - Strengthened local institutional capacity - Early warning systems for educational disruption

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
Overview
This project investigates the causal relationship between international gold price fluctuations and the incidence of social conflicts in mining districts of Madre de Dios, Peru.

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
Research Question
Does the boom in extractive industries fuel social unrest? We exploit exogenous variation in international gold prices combined with local mineral endowments to predict conflict probability at the district level.

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
Methodology
We employ a Shift-Share Instrumental Variable (SSIV) strategy to isolate the component of local economic growth driven purely by external price shocks.
Key equation:
\[
Z_{dt} = \text{Endowment}_d \times \log(\text{Price}_{t})
\]
Where \(Z_{dt}\) is the instrument for district \(d\) at time \(t\).
Data sources: - Ombudsman’s Office (Defensoría del Pueblo): Monthly panel of social conflicts - Sentinel-2 Satellite Imagery: Illegal mining deforestation measurement - Ministry of Economy (SIAF): Local canon transfers analysis

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
Key Findings

A 10% increase in gold prices leads to a 2.5 percentage point increase in the probability of socio-environmental conflict in the subsequent quarter
Effect driven primarily by competition for land rights rather than labor disputes
Impacts concentrated in districts with weak institutional presence

title: Gold Price Shocks and Social Conflict
text:
Implementation

StataPython


* Define Shift-Share Instrument
gen shift_share_iv = gold_endowment * log(gold_price_int)

* Main Specification (Fixed Effects)
reghdfe conflict_dummy shift_share_iv canon_transfers ///
    population_density, ///
    absorb(district_id year_month) ///
    vce(cluster district_id)

* Export Results

title: Higher Education Financing in Peru
text:
Research Question
How can budget allocation be optimized to improve both efficiency and equity in Peru’s public higher education system?

title: Higher Education Financing in Peru
text:
Context
Led analytical work at Peru’s Ministry of Education (MINEDU) to inform resource allocation decisions and policy design for higher education financing.

title: Higher Education Financing in Peru
text:
Methodology
Efficiency Analysis: - Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) for institutional efficiency measurement - Stochastic frontier analysis for robustness checks - Panel data regression with university fixed effects
Equity Analysis: - Concentration curves and Gini coefficients - Theil index decomposition by region and institution type - Spatial distribution analysis
Policy Evaluation: - Regression discontinuity design for reform impact assessment - Difference-in-Differences for performance-based funding effects - Integration of administrative systems (SIAF, SIGA, AIRHSP, NEXUS)

title: Higher Education Financing in Peru
text:
Key Findings

Significant efficiency gaps across universities (average DEA score: 0.67)
Budget concentration favoring Lima-based institutions
Performance-based funding increased research output by 18%
Regional disparities in per-student funding (up to 3x difference)
Economies of scale present in universities with 10,000+ students

title: Higher Education Financing in Peru
text:
Policy Impact
Analysis directly informed budget allocation methodology used in national higher education policy, affecting $800M+ in annual public university funding.
Recommendations implemented: - New formula-based allocation system - Performance incentives for research and graduation rates - Equity adjustments for underserved regions
